items.title: Nvidia May Get A Credit Rating Cut Amid Governance Issues, While US Officials Reportedly Say No Chinese Interference in Huang’s Affair
items.summary: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia on ‘CreditWatch’ with negative implications over governance concerns sparked by Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s rapid exit and return.

items.title: S&P puts NVIDIA on CreditWatch over governance concerns
items.summary: Investing.com -- S&P Global Ratings placed NVIDIA on CreditWatch with negative implications Wednesday, citing concerns about the company's management and governance framework following recent news about its chief executive and potential export control violations.

items.title: CoreWeave Stocks Plunge 10.27% as Credit Markets Price 68% Default Risk
items.summary: CoreWeave's CDS spreads hit a record, implying a 68% five-year default probability, as its bonds fell to record lows.

items.title: S&P Global may sell parts of Capital IQ unit to Cognizant - report
items.summary: Investing.com -- Cognizant (NASDAQ:CTSH) is in talks to take over parts of S&P Global's (NYSE:SPGI) Capital IQ operations in a move that could see around 1,500 employees transfer to the IT services provider, according to a Reuters report citing two people familiar with the matter.

items.title: S&P Global projects 7% growth for India through 2028
items.summary: In its Economic Outlook Asia-Pacific Q1 2027 report, S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI) projects that India will grow at 7% this fiscal year and again in the year to March 2028, a pace that would rank the country among the fastest-expanding economies in the Asia-Pacific region in 2027. According to the outlook, robust expansion will be accompanied by price pressures that refuse to ease.

items.title: S&P Global (SPGI) Stock Looks Fully Valued Based On Earnings Power
items.summary: S&P Global has delivered a 19.4% return over the past three years, and with the stock recently closing at US$455.17, the live question is whether that price lines up with the returns the business earns on the capital it deploys. Over three years, S&P Global has returned 19.4%, which puts real weight on whether those gains are backed by the profitability of the capital invested in its ratings, indices and data operations.
